findings.title: Salesforce service references Prisma without importing it
findings.body: The newly added credential update calls `prisma.credential.update`, but this module has no `prisma` import. This fails TypeScript compilation (`Cannot find name 'prisma'`) and, if type checking is bypassed, throws a `ReferenceError` whenever the Salesforce service initializes.

findings.title: Google refresh persists the Zod parse-result wrapper as the credential key
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a SafeParse result object (`{ success, data }`), unlike the former `googleCredentialSchema.parse` call which returned the credential payload itself. This code stores that wrapper in `Credential.key` at line 100. On the next request `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` receives `{success,data}` rather than Google token fields and rejects the credential, so a successfully refreshed Google integration becomes unusable.

findings.title: HubSpot sync treats a Fetch Response as a HubSpot token object
findings.body: When credential sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the result of `fetch`, i.e. a `Response`, but this caller casts it directly to `HubspotToken` and reads `expiresIn`, `accessToken`, and serializes it into the credential. Unlike the normal HubSpot SDK path, it never calls `response.json()`. Consequently synced HubSpot refreshes produce undefined/invalid token fields and can fail to save a valid credential or authenticate subsequent API calls.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sync uses a Fetch Response as though it were an Axios response
findings.body: The normal refresh callback returns an Axios response with a `.data` payload, but the sync branch in `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a native `fetch` `Response`. The subsequent code reads and mutates `tokenInfo.data` without parsing the response body, so with syncing enabled it cannot obtain an access token and attempts to persist/use invalid values. In addition, the third argument is `credentialId`, which is sent as `calcomUserId`; credential IDs are not user IDs, so the remote app is asked for the wrong user's token.

findings.title: Zoho CRM sync path never parses the remote Fetch response
findings.body: Without syncing this code receives an Axios response and accesses `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data`. With syncing enabled `refreshOAuthTokens` instead returns a native `Response`, and no `.json()` call is made before accessing `.data`. The refreshed credential therefore has no token payload and Zoho CRM calendar operations fail whenever the sync endpoint is used.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh bypasses the configured credential-sync endpoint
findings.body: This new refresh implementation always posts the stored refresh token and app secret directly to Salesforce rather than using `refreshOAuthTokens`. Thus Salesforce is included in the changed integrations but continues to make Cal.com the refresh-token holder/source of truth, contrary to the credential-sync feature; deployments enabling sync cannot refresh Salesforce credentials through their external app store.

findings.title: Salesforce connection is initialized with the expired pre-refresh token
findings.body: After obtaining and saving `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`, the connection is still constructed with `credentialKey.access_token`, which is the token that prompted the refresh. The current request therefore authenticates to Salesforce with the expired token and fails; only a later service construction that rereads the database could use the saved token.

findings.title: Credential-sync token requests contain no authentication
findings.body: The outbound request identifies a user solely by the predictable `calcomUserId` and app slug and sends neither the configured webhook secret nor any signature/authorization header. A self-hosted app-store endpoint has no information with which to distinguish a Cal.com refresh request from an arbitrary caller requesting another user's integration token. The documented secret is only checked on the reverse webhook and does not protect this endpoint.

findings.title: Zoom requests a different app slug than the credential's configured app ID
findings.body: The Zoom callback creates credentials with `appId: "zoom"`, but the refresh-sync request sends `appSlug: "zoomvideo"`. The sync API is explicitly keyed by app slug, so a source application that maps credentials by the configured app ID will not find Zoom credentials and cannot return a refreshed token.

findings.title: Webhook credential upsert is race-prone and can create duplicate credentials
findings.body: The handler implements an upsert as a separate `findFirst` followed by `create`, with no transaction or database uniqueness constraint. Concurrent sync webhooks for the same user and app can both observe no credential and both create one. Multiple credentials for an integration cause nondeterministic `findFirst` selection and leave stale third-party tokens in the database.
